articles.title: Tributes paid to former Healey councillor and firefighter Shaun O’Neill
articles.excerpt: Former Healey councillor and firefighter Shaun O’Neill has died, prompting tributes from colleagues who remember his dedication to public service.
articles.content_html:
Shaun O’Neill, a former councillor for Healey and firefighter, died on 10 November 2026, prompting tributes from colleagues reflecting on his dedication to public service.

Mr O’Neill served as a Labour councillor and was also a representative for the Fire Brigades Union. Colleagues have expressed their sorrow and shared memories of his commitment to the community.

Councillor Shakil Ahmed described him as 'a truly dedicated public servant who gave so much of his life to serving others.'

Councillor Daniel Meredith remembered Mr O’Neill fondly, stating, 'Shaun was a top bloke, a good friend, and someone whose knowledge and experience were second to none.' He highlighted Mr O’Neill’s passion for public service and his commitment to the working people of Rochdale.

The loss of Shaun O’Neill is felt deeply within the community, with many acknowledging his years of service and advocacy. His contributions as both a firefighter and a councillor have left a lasting impact on the Healey area.

Donations are being collected for children aged up to 16 and can be left at various local libraries and leisure centres. Additional collection points include Rochdale Riverside and The Trade Centre UK, making it easier for residents to contribute.

Organised in partnership with local charities and organisations, the appeal encourages the community to shop locally and choose sustainable gifts. Council volunteers will distribute the collected gifts before Christmas Day, ensuring they reach those who need them most.

Requests for help have already been received this year, highlighting the ongoing need for support within the community. The collaborative effort aims to bring joy to local families during the festive period.

Organised by council staff, the appeal has been running for thirteen years and aims to ensure that children living in poverty have presents to unwrap on Christmas morning.

Donations are being accepted until 11 December, with collection points set up at local libraries and leisure centres. Last year, the appeal successfully distributed 10,000 toys to around 3,000 children, highlighting the significant impact it has on the community.

Helen Walton, a council representative, emphasised the importance of donations, stating that every contribution, regardless of size, is appreciated. Requests for assistance have already begun to come in this year, indicating a continued need for support among local families facing financial pressures.

Councillor Rachel Massey has voiced her support for the appeal, underscoring its role in addressing poverty in the borough.

The Christmas Toy Appeal not only provides festive cheer but also encourages community involvement and kindness, making a real difference in the lives of those who need it most.

articles.title: Shortlist announced for Raising Rochdale Education Awards 2026
articles.excerpt: The shortlist for the Raising Rochdale Education Awards 2026 has been revealed, celebrating local educators for their contributions to children's lives.
articles.content_html:
The shortlist for the Raising Rochdale Education Awards 2026 has been announced, recognising the contributions of local educators.

The awards ceremony will take place on Friday, 20 November 2026, at Rochdale Town Hall, celebrating the achievements of teachers, tutors, and support staff who support children and young people.

This year, the event has received a record 896 nominations, reflecting the growing recognition of local educational professionals.

Eighteen awards will be presented, including categories such as Raising Rochdale School or College of the Year, Leadership Team of the Year, Primary Teacher of the Year, Secondary Teacher of the Year, and Post-16 Tutor of the Year.

Andrew Bridson, headteacher of Cardinal Langley RC High School and event organiser, expressed enthusiasm for the event, stating, "We are thrilled to celebrate the incredible work of our educators who make a difference every day in the lives of our children."

The winners will be announced in front of an audience filled with local education professionals, sponsors, family, and friends.

The Raising Rochdale Education Awards, now in its third year, aims to highlight the achievements of those in the education sector and foster a sense of community pride in local schools.

articles.title: Is Rochdale Town Hall haunted?
articles.excerpt: There is no verified evidence that the Town Hall is haunted — but its Victorian courts, an 1883 fire, local poltergeist tales and commercial ghost-hunt events have kept the rumours alive.
articles.summary: There is no verified evidence that the Town Hall is haunted — but its Victorian courts, an 1883 fire, local poltergeist tales and commercial ghost-hunt events have kept the rumours alive.
articles.body:
Short answer: no confirmed haunting has been proved.

Rochdale Town Hall is a Grade I Victorian building with a long, well‑documented civic history; that history — not a stack of authenticated supernatural incidents — is what official records record. The council and the Town Hall’s own conservation pages describe the building’s architect (William Henry Crossland), its opening in 1871, the destructive 1883 fire that brought down the original spire and the major restoration work in the 2020s that reopened previously closed rooms to the public. Those are the facts you can rely on. (Rochdale Borough Council and the Town Hall’s conservation pages do not present any official claims of ghosts.)

So where do the hauntings come from? Two things make the building fertile ground for ghost stories. First, old civic buildings commonly held grim functions: magistrates’ hearings, police business and holding cells have been associated with many town halls across the region, and such associations encourage mobile storytelling about restless spirits. Second, modern interest in the paranormal has been channelled into commercial events. Organisers such as Haunted Happenings advertise overnight “ghost hunts” at Rochdale Town Hall, offering vigils, equipment and guided investigations. Those events are available to book and are the clearest public evidence that people believe the building is worth investigating for ghostly activity — but they are promotions by private operators, not independent, peer‑reviewed proof of anything supernatural.

It is important to separate three things: documented history, local folklore and commercial claims. Documented history (architecture, dates, the 1883 fire, the recent conservation programme) is recorded by the Town Hall and its conservation partners and by national heritage bodies. Local folklore includes older regional tales — Rochdale borough has other well‑known legends and alleged poltergeist cases (for example reported mid‑20th century household disturbances in the Kirkholt area) — but those stories are about people and places across the borough, not verified phenomena inside the Town Hall itself. Commercial claims are where the line blurs: ghost‑hunting companies and enthusiast sites promote investigations and recount experiences, but those accounts are not the same as corroborated evidence assessed by historians or independent investigators.

If you want to check the official record: Historic and civic sources list the building, its architecture and its conservation programme; Rochdale Borough Council and the Town Hall’s visitor pages outline opening times, the recent restoration and the cultural uses of the Great Hall and other rooms. If you want to see the building after dark, private operators run ticketed paranormal events; those operators describe the kinds of activities they run and their booking rules on their commercial pages. Neither the council nor the Town Hall’s official material presents verified sightings, authenticated recordings or formal investigations that demonstrate the presence of spirits.

What this means for locals: you can enjoy the building’s architecture, visit the Great Hall, watch the peregrine falcons nest in the clock tower via the Town Hall webcam, attend a concert or book a wedding there with confidence that the publicly recorded history is well maintained. If you’re tempted by a ghost hunt, treat it as an experience — a themed night in an atmospheric historic setting — rather than settled proof. Where claims are important to people (for example, allegations of harm or historical abuse) always rely on official findings; nothing we found links such matters to hauntings at the Town Hall.

If you’d like to follow up: the Town Hall’s official history and conservation information are the best starting point; the council’s events and visitor pages give current opening arrangements and services. For those curious about local folklore beyond the Town Hall, compiled reports and archives record several separate local poltergeist and haunting tales — interesting as social history, but not evidence of an institutional haunting in the Town Hall itself.

In short: the Town Hall’s drama is historical and architectural. The ghosts are, so far as the record shows, a matter of local legend, private experience and commercial entertainment, not established public fact.

articles.title: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing ranks in top 25% for tenant satisfaction
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing has been recognised for its high tenant satisfaction, ranking among the top landlords in England according to recent government measures.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has been ranked among the top 25% of landlords in England for tenant satisfaction, according to national results released by the Government and the Regulator of Social Housing (RSH).

The Tenant Satisfaction Measures, which assess how well social landlords deliver services to residents, revealed that RBH achieved an overall satisfaction rate of 80.5%, significantly higher than the national average of 74.2%.

Satisfaction with RBH's repairs service was particularly notable, at 85.2%, compared to the national average of 76%.

RBH has pledged to continue improving its services, with a focus on 'being the best landlord it can be'. A spokesperson for RBH stated, "We are proud of our ranking and will strive to enhance our services further to meet the needs of our tenants."

This recognition comes as part of a broader initiative to ensure social housing providers are held accountable for their service delivery. The results of the Tenant Satisfaction Measures are intended to encourage landlords to improve their performance and better meet the needs of their tenants.

articles.title: CEAMS wins national award for sustainable manufacturing innovation
articles.excerpt: The Centre of Expertise in Advanced Materials and Sustainability (CEAMS) has received national recognition for its innovative work in recycling carbon fibre.
articles.content_html:
The Centre of Expertise in Advanced Materials and Sustainability (CEAMS) has won the Sustainability and Circularity Award at the Composites UK Industry Awards for its pioneering work in recycling carbon fibre, marking a significant achievement for the Rochdale-based initiative.

In collaboration with partners including Cygnet Texkimp, SHD Composites, NCC, and Teledyne CML Composites, CEAMS demonstrated a world-first aerospace component made from prepreg material containing 100% recycled continuous carbon fibre.

This innovation proves that recycled carbon fibre can achieve stiffness and strength comparable to virgin materials while utilising existing manufacturing processes.

Rochdale Development Agency, a founding partner of CEAMS, expressed pride in supporting such innovative projects that address real-world challenges. The agency highlighted that this award reinforces Rochdale's growing reputation as a hub for advanced manufacturing and sustainable industry, contributing to the future economy.

Previous research by CEAMS indicated that using recycled continuous carbon fibre could reduce carbon emissions by up to 80% compared to virgin materials.

The award recognises pioneering work that could help transform how carbon fibre waste is reused across the aerospace sector and wider manufacturing industries. Working alongside Cygnet Texkimp, SHD Composites, NCC and Teledyne CML Composites, CEAMS successfully demonstrated a world-first aerospace component manufactured using prepreg material containing 100% recycled continuous carbon fibre. The project showed that recycled carbon fibre can achieve levels of stiffness and strength comparable to virgin material, while using existing industrial manufacturing processes. This creates a realistic route for large-scale adoption across advanced manufacturing sectors. The innovation also offers substantial environmental benefits. Previous CEAMS research estimated that recycled continuous carbon fibre may reduce carbon emissions by up to 80% when compared with virgin material, while helping create more resilient UK supply chains and higher-value uses for composite waste. As a founding partner of CEAMS, Rochdale Development Agency is proud to support innovation that brings together businesses, researchers and industry leaders to solve real-world challenges. This award is further evidence of Rochdale’s growing reputation as a centre for advanced manufacturing, materials innovation and sustainable industry, helping position the borough at the forefront of the technologies shaping the future economy. articles.title: Rochdale Christmas Toy Appeal seeks donations to support local children
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council is calling for donations for its Christmas Toy Appeal, which helps local children in need. Donations are accepted until 11 December 2026.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has launched its Christmas Toy Appeal, urging residents to donate toys for local children living in poverty. The appeal, which has been running annually since 2013, aims to ensure that children have something to unwrap on Christmas morning.

Donations for the appeal can be made until 11 December 2026, at various local libraries and leisure centres across the borough.

Last year, the appeal distributed a record 10,000 toys, highlighting the community's generosity and the increasing need for support among families facing financial pressures during the festive season.

The appeal is organised by the 'Number One Riverside Giving Back' charity, which has been instrumental in coordinating efforts to provide festive cheer to children in need.

The council's initiative is a response to the growing number of requests for help from families, making it crucial for many during the holiday season.

Residents are encouraged to contribute to the appeal, which has been supported by the kindness of the local community. Last year, Holy Trinity CE School collected gifts for the initiative, showcasing the collaborative spirit of the borough.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Christmas toy appeal calls on borough residents to help families in need | Rochdale Borough Council Search Search View menu Accessibility and translate Christmas toy appeal calls on borough residents to help families in need Helen Walton meets some of the team from Renold Gears in Littleborough who donated gifts from customers and staff to boost last year's appeal. Published: 10 November 2026 Rochdale Borough Council’s staff-run charity 'Number One Riverside Giving Back' is now collecting donations for this year’s Christmas Toy Appeal. The appeal helps make sure local children who are living in poverty have presents to open on 25 December 2026. The annual appeal, organised by council staff for the past thirteen years, is accepting donations at local libraries or Your Trust leisure centres until Friday, 11 December 2026. Council policy advisor Helen Walton, from the Giving Back charity said: “Christmas should be a magical time for every child, but for many families the financial pressures they face mean that even a small gift can feel impossible to afford. We’re already seeing requests for help, and that’s why every donation matters. Knowing there’s something to unwrap on Christmas morning will mean the world to a child. We’re incredibly grateful for the continued kindness of our communities, whose support helps bring joy and hope to families when they need it most.” Parents, pupils and staff at Holy Trinity CE School in Littleborough collected gifts for the appeal last year, received by organiser Helen Walton. ‘Every donation matters’ To help, all you need to do is donate an unwrapped, new gift suitable for a child up to 16 years-old and leave it at your local library or Your Trust leisure centre by Friday, 11 December 2026.  There are also lots more collection points across the borough, including Rochdale Riverside retail and leisure destination (management office on first floor), The Trade Centre UK at Sandbrook Park, Rochdale and The Old Police Station in Heywood. Council volunteers, who distributed a record 10,000 toys last year to around 3,000 children will make sure they reach children in time for Christmas Day. Since 2013 the appeal has provided much needed festive cheer for thousands of children and teenagers. Councillor Rachel Massey, cabinet member for children’s services and education at Rochdale Borough Council. Councillor Rachel Massey, cabinet member for children’s services and education at Rochdale Borough Council, said: “No child should feel left out at Christmas, and this appeal helps ensure that thousands of children across our borough can experience the excitement and joy that every young person deserves. Behind every donated gift is a simple act of kindness that can have a lasting impact on a child and their family. I’m incredibly proud of the compassion shown by our communities every year, and I encourage anyone who can help to get involved. Together, we can make this Christmas a little brighter for those who need it most.” As Christmas raises awareness of excess and waste, organisers are encouraging people to shop locally and, where possible, choose sustainable gifts – but above all, every donation, big or small, is really appreciated. You can also order a gift online and send it straight to the appeal. The address is: Giving Back - Christmas Toy Appeal, Rochdale Borough Council, Number One Riverside, Smith Street, Rochdale OL16 1XU. Gifts will need to have been received by Friday, 11 December 2026. One extra gift can make all the difference. Businesses and other organisations supporting the appeal this year include The Trade Centre UK in Rochdale. The appeal is organised by the Number One Riverside Giving Back CIO (1215663) ‘Giving Back’ charity in partnership with Rochdale Borough Council, Rochdale Football Club and Your Trust. Some local businesses and organisations have already stepped up to support the appeal, including STM Agency, Schofield and Sons, Rochdale Football Club, Rochdale Riverside and The Trade Centre UK. articles.title: Dunelm Rochdale shoppers fill store with Christmas gifts for Delivering Joy appeal
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale store says customers have dropped off so many presents in the past week that staff are preparing a count. Gifts go to local causes for people who might otherwise go without.
articles.content_html:
Shoppers at Dunelm's Rochdale store have dropped off so many Christmas presents for its Delivering Joy appeal that staff are preparing to count them up.

The store has thanked customers for the gifts left over the past week, which will go to people in the community who might otherwise go without at Christmas.

In a message to customers, the Rochdale store said: “We’ve had sooooo many gifts dropped off in store over the past week by lots of lovely customers – thank you so much for taking part, you are all so thoughtful & generous! We can’t wait to do a count up to see how many gifts we have now!”

Delivering Joy, which returned on 13 October, is now in its seventh year. Shoppers pick up a gift tag in store, buy a present and leave it at the store, which passes the gifts on to local causes.

Last year the homeware retailer donated nearly 200,000 gifts to more than 1,500 local causes across its stores, according to Dunelm.

Gift bags must be left unsealed so staff can check the contents before the presents are delivered.

If the tags have run out, shoppers can still take part by donating to Age UK, either online at dunelm.com or in store by taking an Age UK bauble to the till and giving anything from £1 to £100.

Source: Dunelm Rochdale and Dunelm, supplied to Rochdale Daily. Photograph: Dunelm Rochdale.

articles.title: Rochdale fighter Owen Webster loses BKFC bout in Glasgow but keeps the town behind him
articles.excerpt: Webster was stopped by Dan Morel in the fourth round at the OVO Hydro on Saturday and has thanked the fans who travelled, saying he will be back better than ever.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale bare-knuckle fighter Owen Webster has thanked the fans who travelled to Glasgow to support him, after losing his BKFC bout to Dan Morel on Saturday night.

Morel won the featherweight contest at the OVO Hydro on Saturday 7 November by technical knockout in the fourth round, stopping Webster 1 minute 17 seconds into the round.

The fight was part of the Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship's BKFC 96 card in Glasgow.

Webster said afterwards: “Nothing in life is easy and if it is it ain't worth it. Saturday night just wasn't meant to be there's no excuses Dan was just the better man on the night and I take my hat off to him.”

He added: “This isn't the end of my journey it's just the beginning theirs a bigger plan for me and I'm sure of that.”

Webster thanked supporters who made the trip to Scotland and those who watched at home, saying: “The love I have for every one of you is unbelievable.”

He also thanked his sponsors for backing him through his fight camps and career, and BKFC for giving him a place on what he called one of the greatest cards in history.

He said he would now take time to heal before returning, adding: “Like I said I'll be back better than ever.”

Sources: Owen Webster, statement supplied to Rochdale Daily; BKFC 96 results. Photograph: supplied.
